chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ays ibn Al-Qasim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding Zakat,

he said: 'Whatever the Banu Umayya take from you, count it as Zakat, and do not give them anything more than what you can manage, for wealth would not remain in this state if you were to pay Zakat twice.'

key_terms.مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ: what you can manage/are able to

ai.seo_question: How should Shia Muslims handle Zakat when the ruling authority takes taxes?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a jurisprudential principle that taxes levied by the Umayyad rulers are deemed equivalent to Zakat, thereby exempting believers from paying it again on the same wealth. This ruling highlights the flexibility of Zakat in Shia jurisprudence, allowing for the substitution of obligatory alms with state-imposed levies to prevent double taxation, provided the amount is sufficient. The hadith underscores the practical application of religious duties under political authority, emphasizing that the intent and receipt of wealth by the ruler fulfill the spiritual obligation.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ays Bin Al Qasim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Zakāt,

so heasws said: ‘Whatever the Clan of Umayya take from you, so reckon with it (as being Zakāt), and do not give them anything what you can (get away with), for the wealth would not remain (but being depleted), if Zakāt were to be paid twice’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn ’Isma’il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from ‘Is ibn al-Qasim

who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Whatever banu ‘Umayyah make you to pay, count it (as Zakat) and do not give anything to them if you can; no assets will be left if you pay twice.’”
